title: Scalar reduction presentations in additive categories
statement: Let A be a preadditive category and B a category, with a functor R:B→A, and n a natural number. A scalar reduction presentation consists of a short exact complex S in A [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence], two objects H,Q of B, maps i:RH→S.X₁ and p:S.X₃→RQ, equations i followed by n times the identity equals zero and n times the identity followed by p equals zero, and proofs that RH→S.X₁→S.X₁ and S.X₃→S.X₃→RQ are short exact. Their middle and first arrows, respectively, are multiplication by n. Specializing R to restriction of integral and residue sheaves gives precisely the extension, Kummer and quotient data used for divisible reduction, including epimorphy on S.X₁ and monicity on S.X₃.

No object is selected by existence: all data and all three short exact sequence proofs are explicit fields. Specialization to the coefficient restriction functor is the previous concrete Presentation record field for field.
